title: Understand a rate as a comparison of different units and find unit rates (240 km in 3 h = 80 km/h)

lesson.title: What a Rate Really Means

steps.say: You already know how to write a ratio like three to two to compare two things of the same kind, such as three red jerseys to two blue ones. Today we look at a special kind of comparison called a rate, where the two things have different units, like kilometres and hours. That is what lets us answer the question: how far does this car go in just one hour?

Imagine your family drives from Vancouver up the highway toward the Interior. In three hours you cover two hundred forty kilometres. Look at that as a table: one column is time in hours, the other is distance in kilometres. Kilometres and hours are different units, so this comparison is a rate, not a plain ratio. Written all together it is two hundred forty kilometres per three hours.

visual.caption: Two different units side by side: hours and kilometres

steps.say: Here is the useful move. A unit rate tells you how much of the top quantity goes with exactly one of the bottom quantity. So we shrink the time column down to one hour, and we shrink the distance the same way. Two hundred forty divided by three is eighty. So in one hour the car covers eighty kilometres, and we say the rate is eighty kilometres per hour. That little word per is doing the work: it means for every one hour.

visual.caption: Same trip, squeezed down to one hour: 80 km

steps.say: Now the mistake I see most often. Some students grab the two numbers and divide three by two hundred forty instead. That gives zero point zero one two five, and honestly that number is not nonsense, but it answers a completely different question: it says each single kilometre takes zero point zero one two five hours. Nobody talks about a road trip that way. So ask yourself what you want one of. You want one hour, so one hour goes on the bottom, and the distance gets divided by three. The unit you want per goes underneath.

visual.caption: Dividing backwards answers a different question: hours per kilometre

steps.say: So whenever you meet a rate, picture that little table, shrink the bottom column to one, and divide in that same direction. Two hundred forty kilometres in three hours is eighty kilometres every hour.

lesson.answer: A rate compares different units, and a unit rate is what you get per one, so divide by the quantity you want one of.

practice.question: Make yourself a small two column table. The left column is Litres of gas and the right column is Cost in dollars. Your one row says forty five litres cost eighty one dollars. What is the unit rate, in dollars per litre?
practice.answer: One dollar eighty per litre. You want the cost for one litre, so litres go on the bottom: eighty one divided by forty five equals 1.80, so the gas is $1.80 per litre. Check it: 1.80 times 45 is 81.
